claim: The new metadata-type guard exits for every referenced generic type, including closed generic classes. Those classes previously went through CollectGeneric and received a formatter in the consuming compilation; now only Cmd gets generated code and Lib.Item<int> has no formatter. This violates the acceptance criterion that closed generic classes keep working as before and can break their AOT serialization.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataGenericClassCompatibilityTests.ClosedGenericClassFromReferencedAssembly_KeepsGeneratedFormatter. It compiles a metadata Lib.Item<T> class reference, runs the generator on the consuming app, and requires a generated implementation of IMessagePackFormatter<Lib.Item<int>>. It passes on base and fails on head because the unconditional OriginalDefinition.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty guard skips collection.

claim: MsgPack005 is silently dropped for a source-declared positional record property with `[property: Key(null)]`. Such a property's declaration syntax is a `ParameterSyntax`, not a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, so `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` returns null. The resulting diagnostic has `Location.None`, and `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` discards it even though the offending member belongs to the current source compilation.

receipt_plan.detail: Run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer over `[MessagePackObject] public partial record MyRecord([property: Key(null)] string Value);` and assert that its analyzer diagnostics include MsgPack005. On head, the property helper returns null and the new location filter suppresses the diagnostic.

claim: The added tests only exercise valid usage declarations and expect zero diagnostics, so they provide no positive control that the new diagnostic filter still reports legitimate diagnostics from the usage compilation. An implementation that discards every diagnostic would satisfy all three added tests.
